summary.headline: Vishnu Chemicals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores, but EBITDA margin slipped to 15.1% from 16.1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating revenue grew 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores and PAT rose 23% to INR39.6 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.1% from 16.1%. Management attributed the sequential moderation to a roughly three-week Vizag maintenance shutdown and a one-off barium baryte price adjustment of close to INR8 crores for the prior two years. Management expects freight costs to stay elevated in Q2 because of West Asia tensions and gave no quarterly or full-year margin guidance, while reiterating a 20% long-term EBITDA margin target. Chromium mix shift, strontium ramp-up and the South Africa chrome mine restart are the main levers cited for H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +24.9% YoY (vs INR346.9 crores in Q1 FY26)
Includes net FX gain of INR11.9 crores, linked to 31% QoQ rise in exports
Nearly full FY26 strontium revenue, per management
Could be upwards of 20% in Q2 per management

segments.name: Barium
segments.commentary: Management says barium runs at optimum utilisation with EBITDA margin expected to stay around 25%; Q1 included a one-off baryte price adjustment of close to INR8 crores. About 70% of barium carbonate is exported, and by-product sulphur prices have risen 300-400%.

segments.name: Chromium (standalone)
segments.commentary: Higher-value derivatives (Chromic Acid, Chrome Oxide Green) were nearly 50% of sales in Q1 vs about 40% in FY26. Standalone gross margin is about 44-45%, with a target of about 50% by year-end.

segments.name: Strontium
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR25 crores in Q1; capacity about 10,000 tonnes running at 50% utilisation, targeted at 65-75% by year-end. Business is EBITDA-positive but below target; input/output ratios remain suboptimal. Main end use is flexible magnets.

segments.name: South Africa chrome mine
segments.commentary: Restart activities under way; production expected around end-July 2026, with volumes to India from H2 FY27 (management also said material flows from Q3). Capex limited to INR20-25 crores.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly or full-year EBITDA guidance given; long-term target of 20% consolidated EBITDA margin reiterated, with management expecting to reach it in FY28.
Barium EBITDA margin expected to stay around 25%; barium volumes expected to grow 15-20% in FY27.
Consolidated margin excluding standalone (barium plus strontium) expected to remain above 20%.
Strontium expected to reach target EBITDA margins by end of FY27; utilisation targeted at 65-75% by year-end.
Chrome metal and DMSO commercial production expected from FY28; total FY27 capex outlay INR200-250 crores (DMSO INR205-240 crores total, INR68 crores spent to 30 June).
Solar capacity to rise from 5 MW to about 20 MW (about 6x), with standalone capex of INR5-6 crores; management estimates 15-20% power cost saving, not yet quantified.
capex_capacity: DMSO: total project capex INR205-240 crores, with about INR68 crores spent to 30 June 2026; import-replacement solvent for pharma and agro.
Chromium derivative expansion: about INR50 crores, including Chrome Oxide Green capacity at Vizag that will use more sodium dichromate.
Barium backward integration line: about INR40 crores to complete.
South Africa mine restart: capex INR20-25 crores; operations expected to start in H2 FY27.
Strontium capacity about 10,000 tonnes, currently at 50% utilisation.
demand_pricing: Revenue mix about 45% domestic and 55% export in Q1.
Ocean freight rates rose sharply because of West Asia tensions; management views these levels as unsustainable and expects normalisation over the medium term.
Logistics cost is a headwind of about 20% of revenue in Q2 per management; the company is trying to pass on part of it and is shifting toward domestic sales in the near term.
Barium benefited from an EU anti-dumping duty on Chinese barium carbonate, adding about 4-5% margin on regular pricing per management.
Leather-segment chrome demand remains challenging; Basic Chrome Sulphate volumes to be reduced sequentially over FY27.

A long-term, take-or-pay supply agreement for Chrome Oxide Green with a European client is expected in the coming months, with formula-linked pricing and fixed volumes for about 10 years; management says it will be margin accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Why did barium margins fall sharply, and what is the sustainable level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a one-off baryte price adjustment of close to INR8 crores for two prior years and said margins should stay around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will strontium margins reach 50% gross margin already?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strontium is still in a stabilisation phase with suboptimal input/output ratios, so the current margin is not normalised; clarity expected over the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any impact from the Vizag maintenance shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no revenue impact because carry-forward inventory was available and volumes lost during maintenance were covered.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the South Africa mine and chrome ore benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Production expected around end-July, with volumes to India from H2 FY27; standalone gross margin of 44-45% expected to move toward 50% by end of FY27, but management declined to quantify the timing precisely.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt is on the books and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Total debt was about INR527 crores at 31 March 2026 (D/E 0.49); management does not disclose quarterly balance sheet figures. FY27 capex planned at INR200-250 crores (per one answer) or about INR360 crores total investment (per a later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% margin achievable next year and is the chrome metal decision linked to the EU contract?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of reaching 20% EBITDA margin in FY28, helped by the Chrome Oxide Green long-term contract, chrome ore integration and product mix; chrome metal to be announced via a strategic partnership, with commercial production from FY28.

risks_watch: Freight and logistics cost: management says logistics could rise to upwards of 20% of revenue in Q2 from 9-10% in Q1, with pass-through only partial and no margin quantification given.

South Africa chrome mine: production start was guided for around end-July 2026 with volumes to India from H2 FY27 (Q3 also cited); gross margin move to 50% depends on this ramp, and the timing was not firmly quantified.
Strontium: utilisation at 50% of about 10,000 tonnes targeted at 65-75% by year-end; gross margin not yet normalised as input/output ratios remain suboptimal.

Capex and debt: FY27 capex was given as INR200-250 crores in one answer and about INR360 crores in another; total debt about INR527 crores at 31 March 2026, with no quarterly balance sheet disclosure until Q2 results.
Chrome metal strategic partnership and Chrome Oxide Green long-term contract: announcement promised soon, but contract quantity and partner details remain under NDA and undisclosed.

Barium margin: management expects around 25% EBITDA margin after a one-off baryte price adjustment of about INR8 crores; sustainability depends on the EU anti-dumping benefit and volume growth of 15-20% in FY27.
key_quotes: We believe such levels are unsustainable, and we expect freight rates to gradually normalize over the medium term.
This will not be a going concern moving forward.
I think we believe the EBITDA margins will continue to remain at 25% moving forward.
We are not giving any guidance for the second quarter or the year as a whole.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story (20% EBITDA margin, barium at about 25%, chrome mix shift) but cautious and evasive on near-term items: no quarterly or full-year guidance, no freight cost quantification, no South Africa mine gross margin timing, and no volume/price split of revenue growth.

adds.what: DMSO import-replacement solvent project (total capex INR205-240 crores; INR68 crores spent to 30 June 2026); commercial production from FY28
Chromium derivative expansion incl. Chrome Oxide Green capacity at Vizag
Barium backward integration line (about INR40 crores to complete)
South Africa chrome mine restart; material flows to India from Q3 / H2 FY27 (capex INR20-25 crores)
Solar capacity from 5 MW to about 20 MW (standalone capex INR5-6 crores)

growth.why: Q1 consolidated revenue rose 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores, and management guides to barium volume growth of 15-20% in FY27 and strontium utilisation rising from 50% to 65-75%, but no company-level revenue or margin guidance was given and Q2 logistics costs are a headwind.
